newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: France calls for determined EU expansion talks.
newsitem.headline: France calls for determined EU expansion talks.

text.p: French Foreign Minister Herve de Charette reiterated France's support on Saturday for the early admission of Central European states to the European Union and said the talks would require political will.
De Charette told a news conference told a news conference France wanted the Czech Republic to join the EU as soon as possible.

"Your interest, it seems, and certainly ours is that this should proceed with determination, not at the pace of experts but at the rhythm of political will," he said at the end of a two-day visit to Prague.
De Charette said on Thursday that France wanted to accelerate the enlargement process and he supported Czech hopes to join the EU by 2000.
EU experts have said the first post-Communist central European states will probably not be able to join before 2002.
The Czech Republic, Hungary and Poland are seen as the leading candidates to join the EU and the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation (NATO).
Talks on enlarging the EU are due to begin in early 1998.
De Charette said much of his time had been devoted to preparations for French President Jacques Chirac's visit to Prague in April.
"The state visit of President Chirac has been fixed for April 2 and 3. I am happy to announce it officially," he said.
